events.title: Eve bears Cain
events.narrative_summary: Adam knows his wife Eve; she conceives and bears Cain, saying she has acquired a man with the LORD.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. Placed about a year after the expulsion (3:23–24), the first union after it, margin 1 year; 9 months allows the pregnancy.

events.title: Eve bears Abel, a herder
events.narrative_summary: Eve bears Cain's brother Abel again. Abel becomes a keeper of sheep and Cain a tiller of the ground.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'She added to bear' (4:2): after Cain, with a guessed gap of one year (margin 1 year). The trades are the brothers' adult occupations and are not dated separately.

events.title: Cain brings fruit of the ground to the LORD
events.narrative_summary: After some time Cain brings an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'At the end of days' (4:3). Radak takes it as a year after Cain began to till; Pseudo-Jonathan gives 14 Nisan. The brothers need to be grown, so set 25 years after Abel's birth, margin 10 years.

events.title: Abel brings firstlings and fat; the LORD regards him
events.narrative_summary: Abel also brings an offering, from the firstborn of his flock and their fat, and the LORD looks with favor on Abel and his offering.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Also' (4:4): the same occasion as Cain's, starting with it; margin 1 day.

events.title: The LORD disregards Cain; Cain burns with anger
events.narrative_summary: The LORD does not look with favor on Cain and his offering. Cain is very angry and his face falls.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Immediately after Abel's offering is accepted (4:4–5): starts at its end; margin 1 day since the text gives no interval.

events.title: The LORD asks Cain why he is angry and warns him
events.narrative_summary: The LORD asks Cain why he is angry and downcast, and tells him that if he does well he will be accepted, but if not sin crouches at the door, and he must rule over it.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A response to Cain's anger (4:5–6): right after it, margin 1 day, a short speech.

events.title: Cain rises against Abel in the field and kills him
events.narrative_summary: Cain speaks to his brother Abel and, when they are in the field, rises up and kills him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time given. Placed a day after the warning, margin 30 days, as the speech 'let us go to the field' suggests a deliberate act, not a continuation of the scene.

events.title: The LORD asks for Abel and curses Cain from the ground
events.narrative_summary: The LORD asks Cain where Abel is; Cain answers that he does not know and asks whether he is his brother's keeper. The LORD says the blood cries from the ground, curses Cain from the ground, and makes him a wanderer.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Starts at the end of the murder, margin 1 day. 'This day' in 4:14 makes 4:9–15 a single day (DAY_SEQUENCE).

events.title: Cain says his punishment is too great
events.narrative_summary: Cain tells the LORD his punishment is too great to bear: he is driven from the ground and hidden from God's face, and anyone who finds him will kill him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: A reply to the sentence in the same scene: 'this day' (4:14), starting where the sentence ends.

events.title: The LORD sets a sign on Cain
events.narrative_summary: The LORD says anyone who kills Cain will be avenged sevenfold, and sets a sign on Cain so that no one who finds him will strike him.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Straight after Cain's plea, in the same scene (4:15).

events.title: Cain leaves the LORD's presence and settles in Nod
events.narrative_summary: Cain goes out from the LORD's presence and lives in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: After the sign, with no gap stated. Duration of 7 days is a rough allowance: Eden's location is not in the registry, so no travel was computed.

events.title: Cain builds a city and names it for Enoch
events.narrative_summary: Cain builds a city and names it after his son Enoch.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The participle 'was building' (4:17) shows ongoing work. Set from a year after Enoch's birth for about 10 years, margin 5 years; the text gives no figures.

events.title: Cain's wife bears Enoch
events.narrative_summary: Cain knows his wife; she conceives and bears Enoch.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: No time word. A year after Cain settles in Nod, margin 1 year; duration allows the pregnancy.

events.title: Enoch's line runs to Lamech
events.narrative_summary: Irad is born to Enoch, Mehujael to Irad, Methushael to Mehujael, and Lamech to Methushael.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Undated genealogy. A span of 320 years, about 80 years per generation over the four births after Enoch's (Irad, Mehujael, Methushael, Lamech; 4:18), is an estimate with no basis in the text; the uncertainty is carried by the margin of the next event.

events.title: Lamech takes two wives, Adah and Zillah
events.narrative_summary: Lamech takes two wives, Adah and Zillah.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Undated. Put 25 years after Lamech's birth (the end of the line event) with a margin of 100 years, reflecting the estimated generation lengths.

events.title: Adah and Zillah bear Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain and Naamah
events.narrative_summary: Adah bears Jabal, father of tent-dwellers and herders, and Jubal, father of harpists and flautists. Zillah bears Tubal-cain, who forges bronze and iron tools, and Naamah.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Undated. Starting two years after the marriage and spread over 15 years to cover four children by two wives; margin 2 years.

events.title: Lamech tells his wives he is avenged seventy-sevenfold
events.narrative_summary: Lamech tells Adah and Zillah that he has killed a man for wounding him, and that if Cain is avenged sevenfold, Lamech will be avenged seventy-sevenfold.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Undated. Placed 10 years after the children's births, margin 10 years; it presupposes the sons grown at most to adolescence.

events.title: Eve bears Seth in place of Abel
events.narrative_summary: Adam knows his wife again; she bears a son and names him Seth, saying God has appointed her another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: The text gives no date, but Gen 5:3 says Adam was 130 when he begat Seth: 130 years from the START of evt.gen_2.man_formed (Adam's formation, the start of his life), Masoretic, REGNAL_YEAR, margin 1 year. Pseudo-Jonathan's 'after 130 years since Abel's killing' is a different count (see reviewer notes).

events.title: Seth has a son and calls him Enosh
events.narrative_summary: A son is born to Seth, and he calls him Enosh.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: Gen 5:6 puts Seth at 105 when he begat Enosh: 105 years from Seth's birth, REGNAL_YEAR, margin 1 year.

events.title: People begin to call on the name of the LORD
events.narrative_summary: Then people begin to call on the name of the LORD.
events.temporal_reasoning_note: 'Then' (4:26) ties it to Enosh's time; set from his birth with a margin of 30 years and a one-year duration as a nominal span.

causal_edges.causal_explanation: The LORD questions and curses Cain because Abel's blood cries from the ground (4:10–11).
Eve names Seth because God has appointed her another offspring in place of Abel, whom Cain killed (4:25).
The LORD's disregard of Cain's offering (4:5) is the response to the offering he brought in 4:3.
The LORD sets a sign on Cain (4:15) in answer to his fear that anyone who finds him will kill him (4:14).
Cain's burning anger and fallen face (4:5) lead him to kill Abel (4:8) despite the warning of 4:7.
The word that Cain would be a wanderer (4:12) is realised when he goes out and dwells in Nod, a name echoing 'wandering' (4:16).
Cain's complaint that his punishment is too great (4:13) answers the sentence of 4:11–12.

entities.summary_bio: The first city named in Scripture, built by Cain and named for his son. Its location is not given.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably a play on the root nad, 'to wander', the word used of Cain's fate in 4:12, 14.
entities.summary_bio: A land east of Eden where Cain settles after leaving the LORD's presence (4:16). Its location is not known.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew hevel, 'breath' or 'vapor'; the same word is used for transience in Ecclesiastes. The text gives no explanation.
entities.summary_bio: Second son of Adam and Eve and a herder of flocks. He brings firstlings of his flock and their fat, the LORD regards his offering, and Cain kills him in the field. Eve names Seth as a replacement for him.
First wife of Lamech, mother of Jabal and Jubal (4:19–21). A different person from Esau's wife Adah in Genesis 26.

entities.etymology_meaning: Eve connects the name with the verb qanah, 'to acquire' ("I have acquired a man with the LORD"); a folk etymology. The noun qayin may also mean 'smith' or 'spear' in related languages.
entities.summary_bio: First son of Adam and Eve and a tiller of the ground. When the LORD regards his brother's offering and not his own, he kills Abel, is cursed from the ground and marked for protection, and settles in Nod, where he fathers Enoch and builds a city.

entities.etymology_meaning: Hebrew Hanokh, probably 'dedicated' or 'initiated', from hanakh 'to dedicate'.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Cain and his wife, born in Nod. Cain names the city he builds after him, and he is the father of Irad in Cain's line (4:17–18).
Son of Seth. In the days of his birth people begin to call on the name of the LORD (4:26).

entities.etymology_meaning: Uncertain; perhaps 'wild ass' or 'city of witness'.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Enoch and father of Mehujael in Cain's line (4:18).

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'stream' or 'he leads', related to the verb yaval; the text gives no explanation.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Lamech and Adah, 'father of those who dwell in tents and keep livestock' (4:20), the ancestor of herdsmen who live in tents.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'stream' or 'ram's horn', from the same root as Jabal; uncertain.
entities.summary_bio: Brother of Jabal, 'father of all who play the lyre and pipe' (4:21), the ancestor of musicians.

entities.etymology_meaning: Uncertain; sometimes taken as 'strong youth' or 'powerful'.
entities.summary_bio: Descendant of Cain, seventh from Adam in Cain's line (4:17–18), who takes two wives, Adah and Zillah. He fathers Jabal, Jubal, Tubal-cain and Naamah, and boasts to his wives of a killing and a vengeance seventy-sevenfold.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'God gives life' or 'smitten by God'; the meaning is uncertain.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Irad and father of Methushael in Cain's line (4:18). The verse spells his name in two forms.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'man of God' or 'man who asks'; the meaning is uncertain.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Mehujael and father of Lamech in Cain's line (4:18).
Daughter of Lamech and Zillah and sister of Tubal-cain (4:22). The text records only her name.

entities.etymology_meaning: From the verb shat, 'to set or appoint': Eve says God has appointed (shat) her another seed in place of Abel.
entities.summary_bio: Third son named in Adam's family, born after Abel's death. Eve names him as the appointed replacement for Abel. He fathers Enosh, in whose time people begin to call on the name of the LORD.

entities.etymology_meaning: Probably 'Tubal the smith', combining a name with qayin, 'smith'.
entities.summary_bio: Son of Lamech and Zillah, who forges all implements of bronze and iron (4:22). His sister is Naamah.

entities.etymology_meaning: Unnamed; the text calls her only 'his wife'.
entities.summary_bio: Cain's wife in the land of Nod. She conceives and bears Enoch (4:17). The text does not say who she was or where she came from.
Second wife of Lamech, mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah (4:19, 22).

components.evidence_explanation: Gen 4:4: the LORD looked to Abel and to his offering.
Gen 4:8: Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him.
Gen 4:2 says Abel was a herder of sheep.
Gen 4:16: Cain dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
Gen 4:14: 'whoever finds me will kill me'.
Gen 4:5: it burned to Cain exceedingly and his face fell.
Gen 4:2 says Cain was a tiller of the ground; 4:12 adds that when he tills it, it will no longer yield its strength to him.
Gen 4:15: sevenfold vengeance on any killer, and the LORD sets a sign for Cain.
Gen 4:11: 'cursed are you from the ground'.
Gen 4:12 and 4:14: 'a wanderer and a fugitive you will be on the earth'.

components.label_value: Calling on the name of the LORD
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 4:26: 'Then it was begun to call on the name of the LORD.'
Gen 4:23: 'I have killed a man for my wound.'
Gen 4:19: Lamech took two wives; the name of one was Adah.
Gen 4:19: the name of the second was Zillah.

components.label_value: Appointed seed in place of Abel
components.evidence_explanation: Gen 4:25: 'God has appointed for me another seed in place of Abel.'

systems.name: Blood vengeance
systems.ancient_near_east_context: In the ancient Near East, killing was answered by the victim's kin or by the community's avenger of blood. Multiples such as seven or seventy-seven express complete and escalating retribution.
rules_and_mechanics: A killer may be pursued and killed in return.
Vengeance can be multiplied to deter, as in the sevenfold decree for Cain.
Lamech claims a seventy-sevenfold vengeance for himself, turning protection into boast.

systems.name: Gift offering to the LORD
systems.ancient_near_east_context: The Hebrew minchah is a gift or tribute, offered by a subordinate to a superior; in Israelite worship it later names the grain offering. Here it is a free offering from the produce of a worker's trade, before any priesthood or law.
rules_and_mechanics: The offerer brings something of his own labour: crops from the ground or firstlings and fat from the flock.
The deity may look on (sha'ah) the offering and offerer, or not.
Acceptance is shown by the deity's regard, not by a stated sign.

systems.name: Protective sign
systems.ancient_near_east_context: A visible sign (ot) is a recurring biblical mark of a divine promise or protection, such as the rainbow or circumcision. The text does not say what Cain's sign is or where it is placed.
rules_and_mechanics: The LORD sets the sign on a person.
The sign serves to deter anyone who finds him from striking him.
It is paired with a warning of sevenfold vengeance on any killer.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Abel brings firstlings of his flock and their fat; the LORD looks on him and his offering.
system_instances.significance_note: The text gives no reason for the difference; Hebrews 11:4 later reads it as faith.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD curses Cain from the ground that received Abel's blood; it will no longer yield to him and he must wander.
system_instances.significance_note: Echoes the curse on the ground in Genesis 3 and turns it against the murderer.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Cain brings some of the fruit of the ground; the LORD does not look on it.
system_instances.significance_note: The first offering in Scripture, and the start of the conflict between the brothers.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD sets a sign for Cain so that no one who finds him will strike him.
system_instances.significance_note: Judgment is joined with mercy: the murderer lives under divine protection.

system_instances.outcome_summary: The LORD declares that anyone killing Cain will be avenged sevenfold.
system_instances.significance_note: Divine vengeance replaces human retaliation in Cain's case; Lamech later quotes it.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Cain names the city he builds after his son Enoch.
system_instances.significance_note: The first city, founded by the wanderer, begins human culture outside the LORD's presence.
Enosh's birth is the moment the text uses to date the beginning of worship.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Lamech takes two wives, Adah and Zillah.
system_instances.significance_note: The first recorded polygamy, departing from the one-flesh pattern of Genesis 2.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Lamech tells his wives that he has killed a man and will be avenged seventy-sevenfold.
system_instances.significance_note: Cain's line grows from protected killer to boasting killer.

system_instances.outcome_summary: People begin to call on the name of the LORD.
system_instances.significance_note: Opens the line of worship from Seth, in contrast to Cain's line of culture and violence.

system_instances.outcome_summary: Eve names her son Seth because God appointed her another seed in place of Abel.
system_instances.significance_note: Marks the continuation of the promised line after Abel's death.

edges.description: Cain tells the LORD that his punishment is too great to bear.
Cain builds a city and names it for his son Enoch.
Cain's wife bears Cain's son Enoch.
Cain rises against his brother Abel in the field and kills him.
Eve conceives and bears Cain, saying she has acquired a man with the LORD.
Eve names her new son Seth, explaining that God has appointed another seed in place of Abel.
The LORD declares Cain cursed from the ground that received his brother's blood.
The LORD does not look to Cain or his offering.
The LORD sets a sign on Cain so that no finder will kill him.
The LORD asks Cain where his brother Abel is.
The LORD looks to Abel and his offering.
The LORD tells Cain that sin crouches at the door and that he must rule over it.
